query: I'm 10 years from retirement. Should I start de-risking now and how aggressively?

recommendations.title: Initiate Gradual Glide Path De-Risking Strategy
recommendations.summary: Begin systematic shift from 60/40 equity/bond allocation toward 50/50 over next 2 years, then 40/60 by retirement at 65.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: With 10 years to retirement and moderate risk tolerance, you're at the optimal inflection point to begin de-risking. Your current 55% equity/35% bond/10% other allocation is appropriate for age 55, but should gradually shift. Research shows aggressive de-risking too early sacrifices growth needed to reach your $1.8M target (current $755K net worth requires 9% annualized growth). Recommend reducing equity exposure by 1% annually for years 1-5, then 2% annually for years 6-10. This maintains growth potential while reducing sequence-of-returns risk as you approach retirement. Your stable income, low debt, and advanced experience support this measured approach rather than dramatic repositioning.
recommendations.suggested_action: Over next 12 months, rebalance to reduce equity allocation from 55% to 53%, increasing bonds from 35% to 37%. Sell $17,000 from VTI/VXUS proportionally and purchase BND.

recommendations.title: Add Target-Date or Balanced Fund for Automatic Glide Path
recommendations.summary: Allocate 15-20% of portfolio to a 2035 target-date fund to automate de-risking and reduce rebalancing burden.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: Your current allocation requires active monitoring and annual rebalancing decisions. A target-date fund (TDF) aligned with your 2034-2035 retirement provides professional, automatic de-risking that becomes more conservative as retirement approaches. This complements your existing holdings (VTI, BND, VXUS) while reducing decision fatigue and behavioral risk. TDFs typically shift from 55% equity at age 55 to 30% equity at retirement—matching your moderate risk profile. Consider Vanguard Target Retirement 2035 (VTTHX) or Fidelity Freedom 2035 (FFTHX), both with expense ratios under 0.15%. This creates a 'core-satellite' approach: TDF provides disciplined glide path while you maintain control over individual holdings for tax-loss harvesting and sector preferences.
recommendations.suggested_action: Allocate $127,500 (15% of $850K assets) to VTTHX by selling proportional amounts from existing ETF positions. Maintain remaining 85% in current holdings.

recommendations.title: Establish Bond Ladder for Retirement Income Certainty
recommendations.summary: Convert 10% of bond allocation ($29,750) into a 5-year Treasury/Municipal bond ladder to create predictable early retirement income.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: Your $80-100K annual retirement income goal requires reliable cash flow beyond portfolio withdrawals. While BND provides bond exposure, it offers variable returns. A bond ladder—buying individual bonds maturing annually from 2034-2038—creates guaranteed income streams for your first 5 retirement years, reducing sequence-of-returns risk during the critical initial withdrawal phase. With your $220K income and likely high tax bracket, consider municipal bonds for tax efficiency, or Treasury bonds for absolute safety. A $30K ladder provides $6K annually in maturity proceeds plus coupon payments, covering 7-8% of target retirement income. This complements rather than replaces BND, which maintains liquidity and flexibility. Your advanced experience and stable finances support this more sophisticated fixed-income strategy.
recommendations.suggested_action: Over next 6 months, sell $29,750 from BND and construct ladder using individual Treasury bonds (2034-2038 maturities) or AA-rated municipal bonds if in high tax bracket. Stagger purchases across 3-6 months.

recommendations.title: Maintain Core Quality Holdings Through Transition
recommendations.summary: Retain individual stock positions (JNJ, UNH, JPM, BRK.B, PG) as they provide quality, dividends, and downside protection during de-risking phase.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: Your 15% allocation to individual stocks (JNJ, UNH, JPM, BRK.B, PG) represents high-quality, dividend-paying companies with defensive characteristics ideal for pre-retirement portfolios. These companies average 2-3% dividend yields, providing income that supplements bonds while maintaining equity upside. Healthcare (JNJ, UNH) offers recession-resistance; financials (JPM, BRK.B) benefit from rising rates; consumer staples (PG) provide stability. All have 20+ year dividend growth records, supporting your income generation goal. While conventional wisdom suggests eliminating individual stocks during de-risking, these specific holdings reduce rather than increase portfolio risk compared to pure index exposure. Their combined volatility is lower than VTI alone. Maintain these positions; avoid the urge to 'clean up' the portfolio prematurely. Only rebalance if any single position exceeds 5% of total portfolio.
recommendations.suggested_action: Hold all current positions. Monitor quarterly but avoid selling unless fundamental deterioration or individual position exceeds 5% of portfolio. Reinvest dividends into BND to support gradual bond allocation increase.
